self_review.verdict: OK — no blocking findings; fix is a genuine harness defect repair, no test weakened/disabled/deleted, no implementation bug found in StepExecutor/engine.

root_cause.evidence: Temporary debug print on the crash test showed sentCount=0, status=completed, reqCount=0 — ZERO Telegram requests, yet the execution completed. So the 400 for block-3 was 'not consumed' only because NO send ever happened; the step was never executed. The auditor's 'MockWebServer QueueDispatcher / send-count interaction' hypothesis was the symptom, not the cause.
root_cause.mechanism: The seed helper multiTextMessage(id, next, texts...) called s.setId("m"). FunnelExecutionEngine.graphMode(snapshot) probes snapshot.get(0).getId() != null → a non-null first-step id flips the snapshot into GRAPH mode. But seedExecution() seeds only currentStepIndex=0 and never sets currentStepId. In graph mode currentStep()/endOfGraph() treat a null currentStepId as the explicit 'End' marker (FunnelExecutionEngine.java:351-354, 387-388), so the engine completed the run WITHOUT executing step 0 → zero sends. The single-block sendMessage() helper (which passes) sets NO id, so its runs stay in index-drain mode and execute step 0 correctly.
root_cause.why_unit_green_but_IT_red: FunnelStepExecutorTest (default lane) calls StepExecutor.message() directly, bypassing the engine's currentStep() cursor resolution, so the graph/index mismatch never surfaced there — confirming the engine send-loop and crash semantics are correct; only the IT seeding was wrong.

fix.summary: Split the multiblock seed helper by navigation mode so each test seeds a consistent cursor. Index-seeded tests (seedExecution, drives by currentStepIndex) now use a new id-less helper multiTextMessageIndexed(String...); the graph-mode snapshot-isolation test keeps multiTextMessage(id, next, String...) with seedGraphExecution (which sets currentStepId). Shared block-builder multiTextMessageBlocks() avoids duplication.
fix.overload_ambiguity_guard: Used a DISTINCT name (multiTextMessageIndexed) rather than a multiTextMessage(String...) overload: a call like ("b1","b2","b3") would bind to the MORE-SPECIFIC (String,String,String...) id-setting variant under Java varargs overload resolution and silently re-introduce the graph-mode mismatch. Documented inline.
fix.invariant_proof_preserved: Per-node at-most-once is asserted by send-count ACROSS TWO TICKS (crash test: sentCount==3 after tick 1, still ==3 after the second sweep — terminal-failed row never re-claimed, no replay), not by status alone. Happy-path asserts exactly 3 sends in one tick.
